question.problem: Which curve is defined by the equation $9{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}=10?$
question.worked_solution:
Consider the quadratic form $Q(x)=9{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+6{x}_{2}^{2}.$ To determine the curve defined by the given equation, we reduce $Q(x)$ to its canonical (diagonal) form.  

First, we write down the matrix of $Q(x),$ which is

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & 2 \\ 2 & 6\end{aligned}].
$$

Next, we find the eigenvalues of $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}9-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 6-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-15\lambda +50 & =0 \\ \lambda  & =5,\,10\end{aligned}
$$

So, our quadratic form can be reduced to $5{y}_{1}^{2}+10{y}_{2}^{2}.$ 

In the new variables, the curve has the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}5{y}_{1}^{2}+10{y}_{2}^{2} & =10 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{2}+\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{1} & =1 \\ \frac{{y}_{1}^{2}}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}}+\frac{{y}_{2}^{2}}{1} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

This is an ellipse with semiaxes $\sqrt{2}$ and $1.$
